title: Coordinate boundary data with projective finite-fibre structure
statement: Under the hypotheses of lem-fin-projective-coordinate-boundary, there are a nonempty principal open D(a) and a closed subset T of the pullback of Y to D(a), with the exact prescribed complement support, such that the vanishing-ideal subscheme morphism to D(a) is projective, D(a) is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, and every geometric fibre is finite.

source.place: Proof steps 1-5, with the final finite-morphism step isolated for the parent node

proof.text: For every dense coordinate open, choose a nonzero polynomial in the ideal of its closed complement, invert the product of leading coefficients, and make the polynomials monic. On each affine chart of the reduced boundary these monic equations give a finite spanning family after every geometric base change, hence finite geometric fibres.

The reduced boundary is a closed subscheme of the projective base change, hence projective; the principal open of the Noetherian integral affine base is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. The coordinate-chart computation supplies the exact support equality and the stated geometric-fibre finiteness.
